title: Functional groups
summary: Learn about alcohols, ethers, aldehydes, ketones, acids, esters, amines and amides.
cards.0.p: The group of atoms that decides a compound's reactions and properties is called a functional group. The carbon skeleton is the carrier, and the group gives the character. In formulas, R is the hydrocarbon part.
cards.0.svg#12: R−OH: R is the hydrocarbon part,
cards.0.etk.soru: Match each functional group with its compound class (R: hydrocarbon part).
cards.0.key: Compounds with the same functional group undergo similar reactions.
cards.1.p: If an −OH group is bonded to a saturated carbon, the compound is an alcohol. Ethanol and 2-propanol are examples. If the carbon carrying −OH is bonded to 1, 2 or 3 carbons, the alcohol is 1°, 2° or 3°.
cards.1.svg#0: Red C: the carbon bonded to −OH
cards.1.key: An alcohol's name is made by adding -ol to the alkane name. In phenol, −OH is bonded to a benzene ring, and in acetic acid, it is bonded to the C=O carbon. So neither is an alcohol.
cards.1.once.soru: Why does the name of ethanol (C₂H₅OH), the alcohol in cologne, end in -ol?
cards.1.once.secenekler.0.neden: Alcohol names are made by adding -ol to the alkane name.
cards.1.once.secenekler.1.neden: There is no O₂ gas in the molecule. The O atom is inside the −OH group.
cards.1.once.secenekler.2.neden: The name comes from the group, not from the state of the substance.
cards.2.p: Alcohols form hydrogen bonds between their −OH groups. That is why they boil at much higher temperatures than similar alkanes. They also form hydrogen bonds with water, but solubility drops as the chain gets longer.
cards.2.key: Aqueous solutions of alcohols are neutral. An alcohol gives H₂ with Na (2C₂H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂), but an ether does not.
cards.3.p: Oxidizing agents remove the H of −OH and one H on the same carbon. A 1° alcohol becomes an aldehyde (−CHO) first, then a carboxylic acid (−COOH). A 2° alcohol becomes a ketone (C=O). A 3° alcohol is not oxidized.
cards.3.svg#16: not oxidized (no H on that C)
cards.3.key: KMnO₄ and K₂Cr₂O₇ are oxidizing agents. Ethanol becomes ethanal first, then acetic acid. 2-propanol becomes acetone.
cards.4.p: Ethanol is made when yeast breaks down sugar without oxygen. This process is called fermentation. Methanol is very toxic, and even a small amount can cause blindness or death.
cards.4.key: In the body, methanol turns into formaldehyde and formic acid. It cannot be told apart from ethanol by smell or look. The poison in bootleg liquor is also methanol.
cards.4.once.soru: When yeast is added to dough, the dough rises. What forms as the yeast breaks down sugar?
cards.4.once.secenekler.0.neden: In fermentation, sugar turns into ethanol and CO₂. The CO₂ makes the dough rise.
cards.4.once.secenekler.1.neden: Yeast does not make methanol. The product of fermentation is ethanol.
cards.4.once.secenekler.2.neden: A gas makes the dough rise, and that gas is CO₂.
cards.5.p: Alcohols with more than one −OH are polyhydric alcohols. Ethylene glycol (2 OH) is antifreeze and is toxic. Glycerol (3 OH) holds moisture and is part of the structure of fats.
cards.5.key: The more −OH groups, the higher the boiling point. Fat = glycerol + 3 fatty acids.
cards.5.once.soru: In winter, what is added to the water in a car radiator to keep it from freezing?
cards.5.once.secenekler.0.neden: Ethylene glycol lowers the freezing point of water and is the main ingredient of antifreeze.
cards.5.once.secenekler.1.neden: Salt also delays freezing, but it makes metal rust.
cards.5.once.secenekler.2.neden: Sugar is not used in radiators, because it settles out and clogs them.
cards.6.p: In an ether, an O atom links two carbon groups (R−O−R′). An ether has no O−H bond, and its molecules do not form hydrogen bonds with each other. Ethanol and dimethyl ether are functional group isomers of each other.
cards.6.key: Diethyl ether is a volatile, highly flammable solvent. Aldehyde–ketone and acid–ester pairs can also be functional group isomers.
cards.7.h: Aldehydes and ketones: the carbonyl group
cards.7.p: The C=O group is called a carbonyl. At the end of a chain (−CHO), it makes an aldehyde, and between two carbons, it makes a ketone. Their names end in -al (ethanal) and -one (propanone).
cards.7.key: Formalin is a 37% solution of methanal. Acetone (propanone) is used as nail polish remover.
cards.7.once.soru: The acetone in nail polish remover is a ketone. Where is the C=O in a ketone?
cards.7.once.secenekler.0.neden: In a ketone, the carbonyl carbon has a carbon on each side.
cards.7.once.secenekler.1.yazi: At the end of the chain
cards.7.once.secenekler.1.neden: A C=O at the end (−CHO) is an aldehyde.
cards.7.once.secenekler.2.neden: Acetone is a three-carbon molecule with no ring.
cards.8.p: Aldehydes are easily oxidized, and ketones are not. Tollens' reagent gives a silver mirror with an aldehyde. Blue Fehling's solution gives a brick-red precipitate with an aliphatic aldehyde.
cards.8.key: Benzaldehyde gives a positive Tollens test but not a Fehling test. In the test, the aldehyde is oxidized to a carboxylic acid.
cards.9.p: Compounds with a carboxyl group (−COOH) are called carboxylic acids. Formic acid in ants and acetic acid in vinegar are examples. They are weak acids. With bases, they give a salt and water, and with active metals, they give H₂.
cards.9.svg#5: weak acid: equilibrium lies far to the left
cards.9.key: Their names end in -oic acid, as in ethanoic acid. They give CO₂ with carbonates. Because its structure resembles an aldehyde, HCOOH also gives a positive Tollens test.
cards.9.once.soru: Vinegar fizzes when you add a little carbonate. Which group does the acid in vinegar carry?
cards.9.once.secenekler.0.neden: The carboxyl group gives off H⁺. So the carbonate releases CO₂ foam.
cards.9.once.secenekler.1.neden: An alcohol's −OH group is neutral and does not make carbonate fizz.
cards.9.once.secenekler.2.neden: The aldehyde group is not an acid.
cards.10.p: When a carboxylic acid and an alcohol are heated with concentrated H₂SO₄, an ester and water form. The reaction is reversible, and the reverse is called ester hydrolysis. Small esters smell like fruit.
cards.10.svg#17: Water: the acid's −OH + the alcohol's H
cards.10.key: An ester's name gives the alcohol's alkyl group first, then the acid with the ending -oate, as in ethyl ethanoate. Isoamyl acetate smells like bananas, and ethyl butanoate like pineapple.
cards.11.p: Fats are esters formed from the three −OH groups of glycerol and three fatty acids. When a fat is heated with NaOH, glycerol and soap form. This process is called saponification.
cards.11.svg#13: The tails sink into the dirt, and the heads face the water.
cards.11.key: 1 mol of triglyceride is saponified by 3 mol of NaOH. KOH gives a softer soap.
cards.12.p: Amines are derivatives of ammonia in which carbon groups replace the H atoms, and they are weak bases. In an amide, N is bonded to a carbonyl carbon (−CONH−). The peptide bond in proteins is an amide bond.
cards.12.key: The formula of methylamine is CH₃NH₂. When an amine and a carboxylic acid combine, an amide and water form. A peptide bond also forms with the loss of water.
cards.12.once.soru: The bad smell of fish comes from amines. Squeezing lemon on it reduces the smell. Why?
cards.12.once.secenekler.0.yazi: The acid forms a salt with the amine
cards.12.once.secenekler.0.neden: An amine is a base, and the acid in lemon turns it into a salt that does not evaporate.
cards.12.once.secenekler.1.neden: The lemon smell helps, but the main effect is that the amine turns into a salt.
cards.12.once.secenekler.2.neden: Lemon does not cook the fish. The acid in lemon neutralizes the basic amine.
cards.13.p:
• The functional group decides a compound's properties.
• A 1° alcohol becomes an aldehyde first, then an acid. A 2° alcohol becomes a ketone, and a 3° alcohol is not oxidized.
• Aldehydes give a positive Tollens test, and ketones do not.
• An acid and an alcohol give an ester and water. A fat and NaOH give soap.
• An amine is a base, and a peptide bond is an amide bond.
quiz.0.q: Propanoic acid and methanol are heated with concentrated H₂SO₄. Which ester forms?
quiz.0.e: An ester's name gives the alcohol's alkyl group (methyl) first, then the acid with -oate (propanoate). So CH₃CH₂COOCH₃ is methyl propanoate.
quiz.0.y.0: You reversed the order. The alkyl part comes from the alcohol (methyl), and the -oate part from the acid (propanoate).
quiz.0.y.2: The acid has 3 carbons (propanoic). Ethanoate comes from a 2-carbon acid.
quiz.0.y.3: The alcohol is methanol. So the alkyl part is methyl, not propyl.
quiz.1.q: How many grams of NaOH are used when 0.2 mol of triglyceride (fat) is completely saponified? (NaOH = 40 g/mol)
quiz.1.e: Each triglyceride has three ester bonds, so 1 mol of fat uses 3 mol of NaOH. 0.2 × 3 = 0.6 mol of NaOH is needed. That is 0.6 × 40 = 24 g.
quiz.2.q: Sort each alcohol by the first product it forms when oxidized with K₂Cr₂O₇.
quiz.2.e: Ethanol and 1-propanol are primary alcohols and become aldehydes first. 2-propanol and 2-butanol are secondary alcohols and give ketones. (CH₃)₃C−OH is a tertiary alcohol. The carbon carrying −OH has no H, so it is not oxidized.
quiz.3.q: X and Y both have the formula C₃H₆O. X gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent, and Y does not. What could X and Y be?
quiz.3.o.1: X and Y are the same compound
quiz.3.e: A silver mirror points to an aldehyde (propanal). A ketone (propanone) does not give a positive Tollens test. The two are functional group isomers with the same formula. The formula of 2-propanol is C₃H₈O.
quiz.3.y.0: Tollens' reagent oxidizes aldehydes. Propanone is a ketone, so it gives no silver mirror.
quiz.3.y.1: The same compound gives the same reaction. Different behavior shows two separate isomers, an aldehyde and a ketone.
quiz.3.y.2: The formula of 2-propanol is C₃H₈O, and it gives no silver mirror. Propanal does give a silver mirror.
A:ozet: Add a group to ethane and dissolve alcohols in water. Compare ethanol with an ether, oxidize alcohols, test an aldehyde, then make an ester and soap.
A:adimlar.0.metin: Put different groups in place of one H in ethane. Turn ethane into a liquid that mixes with water.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.ipucu: Which group can form hydrogen bonds with water?
A:adimlar.0.gorev.tamam: The −OH that replaced an H turned gaseous ethane into ethanol. Ethanol boils at 78 °C and mixes with water in any proportion. This is because the −OH group forms hydrogen bonds with water.
A:adimlar.1.metin: An alcohol's −OH end is polar, and its carbon chain is nonpolar. Lengthen the chain and watch the solubility in water. Find the longest alcohol that mixes with water in any proportion.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.ipucu: Look for the last alcohol whose bar stays blue.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.tamam: Alcohols up to propanol mix with water in any proportion. From butanol on, solubility drops quickly.
A:adimlar.2.metin: Ethanol and dimethyl ether both have the formula C₂H₆O. So they are functional group isomers. Compare them with the switch.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.soru: Why does ethanol boil at a much higher temperature?
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.0.yazi: Ethanol has a larger molar mass
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Both have the formula C₂H₆O, and their molar masses are the same (46 g/mol).
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.1.yazi: Ethanol molecules hold each other by hydrogen bonds
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Ethanol's O−H group forms a hydrogen bond with the O atom of a neighboring molecule. The ether has no O−H, and its molecules attract each other weakly.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.2.yazi: The bonds between atoms in the ether are weak
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Boiling does not break the bonds inside a molecule. What is overcome is the attraction between molecules.
A:adimlar.3.metin: Orange dichromate removes the H of −OH and one H on that carbon, and turns green itself. We add a primary, a secondary and a tertiary alcohol to three tubes.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.soru: In which tube does the orange color stay?
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Ethanol is a primary alcohol, and its carbon carrying −OH has 2 H. It is oxidized first to ethanal, then to acetic acid.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: 2-propanol is a secondary alcohol, and its carbon carrying −OH has 1 H. It is oxidized to propanone (acetone).
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: In a tertiary alcohol, the carbon carrying −OH has no H. With no H to remove, it is not oxidized under these conditions.
A:adimlar.4.metin: Aldehydes are easily oxidized, and ketones are not. Heat the three tubes first with Tollens' reagent, then with Fehling's solution, and compare the results.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Benzaldehyde is an aldehyde and gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Propanal is an aliphatic aldehyde and gives both tests.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Propanone is a ketone, and its carbonyl carbon has no H to remove. So neither a silver mirror nor Cu₂O forms.
A:adimlar.5.metin: An acid and an alcohol give an ester and water. An ester's name gives the alcohol's alkyl group first, then the acid with the ending -oate. Choose the acid and the alcohol to make ethyl butanoate, which smells like pineapple.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.ipucu: The first part of the name comes from the alcohol (ethyl), and the second from the acid (butanoate).
A:adimlar.5.gorev.tamam: Butanoic acid and ethanol give ethyl butanoate and water. The reaction is reversible, and water can break the ester back down. This is called ester hydrolysis.
A:adimlar.6.metin: In a fat, glycerol is linked to three fatty acids by ester bonds. NaOH breaks each ester bond. Saponify 1 mol of fat completely, with no NaOH left over.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.ipucu: How many ester bonds are there?
A:adimlar.6.gorev.tamam: 1 mol of triglyceride and 3 mol of NaOH give 1 mol of glycerol and 3 mol of soap. Soap is the sodium salt of a fatty acid.
A:kapanis.0: The functional group decides a compound's character. A single −OH added to ethane turns this gas into a liquid that mixes with water.
A:kapanis.1: The first three alcohols mix with water in any proportion. As the chain gets longer, solubility drops.
A:kapanis.2: Ethanol and dimethyl ether are functional group isomers. Ethanol forms hydrogen bonds, so it boils at a much higher temperature.
A:kapanis.3: A 1° alcohol becomes an aldehyde first, then an acid. A 2° alcohol becomes a ketone. A 3° alcohol is not oxidized.
A:kapanis.4: Aldehydes give a positive Tollens test, and ketones do not. Benzaldehyde, however, does not give a positive Fehling test.
A:kapanis.5: An acid and an alcohol give an ester and water. 1 mol of fat is saponified by 3 mol of NaOH.
